answer: A beacon attestation chain makes each identity pay for its history: a new agent can only join the economy after a chain of verified paid tasks vouches for it, so a sybil farm must fund a real work record for every clone. A trellis of mutual vouching then ties each agent to several independent sponsors, and any sponsor caught vouching for a fake loses its stake. Yarrow-like slow growth caps how fast reputation can accumulate, so spinning up a thousand identities in a day buys nothing. The attacker cost becomes the full price of genuine work per identity, not the price of one copy.
